lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: everyday examples of conditional probability and independence
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: everyday examples of conditional probability and independence

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: P(A and B) = 3/20, P(B) = 5/20. Find P(A|B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 4/20, P(B) = 8/20, and P(A and B) = 3/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A box holds 10 items, of which 4 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 42/100 and P(B) = 90/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 29/100, P(B) = 27/100, and P(A and B) = 20/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.
The two events are mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A box holds 16 items, of which 7 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 7/100 and P(B) = 8/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
